title: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
summary: GATT was a set of multilateral trade agreements aimed at abolishing quotas and cutting tariffs. Concluded by 23 countries at Geneva in 1947, it took effect provisionally on 1 January 1948 and, through successive rounds, drove trade liberalization until the World Trade Organization replaced it in 1995.

as_recorded.value: DONE at Geneva, in a single copy, in the English and French languages
Entry into force for Australia and generally: 1 January 1948 (provisionally)
GATT went out of existence with the formal conclusion of the Uruguay Round on April 15, 1994.

importance.justification: Framework that liberalized world trade for decades and led to the WTO.
